To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
injected TFF1 and 3 bind to TTF2-immunorective cells in the gastrointestinal mucosa in rats.
the TFF peptides are taken up by the same cells in the GI mucosa and that TFF3 is taken up to a greater extent than TFF1.

the trefoil factor peptides TFF1, T2 and T3 are taken up by cells in the mucus-producing glands of the gastrointestinal tract and are subsequently transported to the mucous neck cells, which secrete them into the mucus layer, where they are believed to interact and stabilize the mucus gel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the localization and metabolism of TFF1, TTF2 and TFF 3 in the rat.
the interaction between TFFs and mucins, and we have shown that TFFs can interact with the mucous neck cells in the stomach.
the role of TFFs in the gastrointestinal mucous barrier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TFF1, TTF3, and TFF2 bind to the same cell types in the GI tract.
injected TFF1 and 3 monomers and dimers bind to TFF1- and TFF2-immuno-reactive cells in the gastrointestinal mucosa in rats.
TFF1 and 3 bind to TFE2-positive cells, but not to TFF1 and/or TFF3-positive cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TFFs are secreted into the lumen, and the binding to the cells is a part of their function.
injected TFFs are taken up by the TFF2-immunoactive cells and that the TFF2 cells have a receptor-like activity to TFF1 and -3.
the TFF peptides, TFF1, TTF2 and TFF2 are co-secreted and co-localized with the mucus in the GI tract and that they interact with each other to form a stable gel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
injected TFFs bind to TFF1/TFF2/TFF3 immunoreactivity in the GI tract and are taken up into the mucus layer.
TFFs are taken up by the TFF2-immunoactive cells in the GI mucosa.
TFF2 is the key peptide in the GI tract, as it is the one that interacts with the TFF-binding cells, and that it is TFF2 that binds to the TFF-binding cell receptors.
